per_hours_basis: 100 full-time employees x 40 h/week x 50 weeks = 200,000 h

per_hours_source.citation: OSHA guidance on calculating incidence rates for the Form 300/300A (copy hosted by NJ Dept. of Labor): https://www.nj.gov/labor/safetyandhealth/assets/PDFs/Survey/form300.pdf
per_hours_source.note: The 200,000-hour basis and the rate formulas are OSHA guidance, not text of 29 CFR 1904.

aggregation.rule: ratio of sums: sum cases (or days) over establishments, divide by sum of hours, times 200,000
aggregation.source: Programme convention (ehs-osha-analysis metrics.py module docstring); not a regulatory requirement.

metrics.name: Total Recordable Incident Rate
form_300a_columns: I job transfer or restriction cases

metrics.name: Days Away, Restricted or Transferred rate
form_300a_columns: I job transfer or restriction cases

metrics.name: Lost Time Incident Rate (days-away cases only; OSHA DAFWII)
metrics.note: Industry use of LTIR varies; some include restricted-duty cases, which makes it DART. This programme uses days-away only.

metrics.name: Severity rate (days lost per 200,000 hours)
form_300a_columns: L total days of job transfer or restriction
metrics.note: Days away are capped at 180 per case when the employer uses the 1904.7(b)(3)(vii) cap, so this rate is bounded per case.

metrics.name: Fatality rate per 200,000 hours
metrics.note: TypeScript only; the Python package folds deaths into TRIR and has no separate rate.

denominator.definition: Total hours worked by all employees covered by the OSHA 300 Log (actual hours, not scheduled)
denominator.note: Workers not on the payroll but supervised day-to-day are covered by the log (1904.31); ehs-benchmarks exposes this as contractorBasis 'combined' vs the default 'employee-only'. Undefined when hours <= 0: TypeScript returns null, Python returns NaN; both mean 'not computable', never 0.
